references.text: Parallel text in Exodus containing the same commandment against worshipping idols, with nearly identical wording describing God as a jealous God who punishes the fathers' sins on the children.
The Lord's self-revelation to Moses where He declares that He visits the fathers' sins on children and grandchildren to the third and fourth generation.
Describes the Lord as a jealous God (El Kanna), the same description used in Deuteronomy 5:9.
Repeats the principle that the Lord visits the fathers' sins on the children to the third and fourth generation.
Describes the Lord as a consuming fire and a jealous God, the same theme of God's jealousy.
Warns again that the Lord is a jealous God and His wrath can be kindled.
Joshua describes the Lord as a holy and jealous God who will not forgive sin and transgression.
Jeremiah prophesies that people shall no longer say, 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge,' commenting on the principle in Deuteronomy 5:9.
Ezekiel addresses the proverb about the fathers' sins and the children's punishment, explaining that each soul will be held accountable for its own sin.
Nahum describes the Lord as a jealous and avenging God.
